HELD. I traced the whole chain first-hand. Obj_OreDeposit.as:80-87 clearOre() calls StageManager.addToDeadList(objectName) - the call is on line :83, not :82 as the finding writes, but it is inside its own cited range. StageManager.as:621-627 pushes onto roomDeadList; GameStage.as:602-632 createRoomObjects sets skipFlag for any object whose name is in the list; roomDeadList is cleared at :249 (initRooms) and :366 (node change) and NOWHERE else - I checked every reference, and :451, the within-node room change, passes roomDeadList to createRoomObjects WITHOUT clearing it, which is exactly what makes the rule per-node rather than per-room. new_findings.text: The WEB v0.717 build carries the whole stage-fit model on disk, and it names all three numbers the ui-hud lane has been arguing about. 1t1540s0.as:271-273 declares originalWidth 800, originalHeight 480, originalHeightWithBar 690 - so the 690 in the payload SWF header is the FRIEND-BAR stage variant, taken only when the browser viewport aspect is <= 800/690 = 1.1594 (:277), and the game canvas is 800 x 480. :295-307 then picks fit-width (offsetX 0, letterbars) or fit-height (offsetX = (stageWidth - 800*scale)/2, pillarbars) and writes scale/offsetX/offsetY/fitWidth into 1t1523s0.1t9358s0/9359/9360/9361, which 1t113s0.as:375 consumes to convert mouse coords into game space. This CONFIRMS REBUILD_READINESS.md:117 and :171 from a web artifact, kills the 800x690 overturn, and supplies the mechanism the aspect-ratio blocker asked for. The only thing still per-video is the BRANCH, since the viewport aspect is not recorded anywhere.

new_findings.text: The single sentence RR:158 rests on - the on-screen 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' - is not a lock notice, it is the reload/crit meter's own low-end label, and the web build shows it switching. 1t113s0.as:110-111 builds two htmlText strings: a black one from getString(175) ('Critical Hit') and a GREY (#BBBBBB) one from getString(960). :328-358 computes ratio = (reload-48)/(maxreload-48) clamped at 0, then shows the grey label exactly when ratio == 0, HIDES it while 0 < ratio < 1, and swaps to the black 'Critical Hit' plus Snd_criticalDamage at ratio >= 1. The gate the stance button asks (1t99s0.as:3048-3051) is the same threshold, reload >= 48. String 960 does not exist in the v0.682 table (docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json has no key 960), i.e. it is a v0.717 addition - which is also why the label has never been sourced. So one bar drives three states: below 48 'cannot change stance', above 48 stance switching is legal, at max the crit fires.

Also: gracePeriod is a flat 900 s (:55), and the 12-hour crop (case 4, :160-169) has no rot branch at all.

new_findings.text: The real web v0.717 nameplate rule, which the packet's nameplate finding states as a colour split. 1t122s0.as (the web EnemyPlayer) has an if/else at every plate write: :92-99, :802-809, :917/:921 and :1418/:1422, all of the form `if(level > 0 && !this.1t4895s0()) { name + " (" + level + ")" } else { name }`. Android v0.682 EnemyPlayer.as:84, :776 and :881 have NO else branch - they always format the level in. Meanwhile the RED overworld aggro plate carries the same lvl==0 split in BOTH builds (1t8638s0.as:79-86 / Obj_NPCAggro.as:74-81). So the rule is 'append (N) iff level > 0', not 'red carries it, white does not', and the change is a v0.717 addition on the duelist/boss path only. 1t4895s0 (:1763-1766) is a spectator-mode predicate, not a level predicate.

new_findings.text: REBUILD_READINESS.md:155-157 labels 0.9/1.2/1.4 'MASTERY-9 CEILING values' and offers a decide-and-flag 'the build targets mastery-9'. The ceiling is 10. Each of the three stance-mastery skills declares exactly ten <level> rows: skilldata.xml:4 is <id>1000</id> and its tenth level value is at :74, :83 is <id>1001</id> with its tenth at :153, and skill 1002's tenth is at :232. The achievement copy says it in words: strings.json["8131"] = 'Light Stance Mastery Level 10.', ["8132"] and ["8133"] the same for Balanced and Heavy. Put mastery = 10 into the web formulas (1t99s0.as:3262/:3265) and you get exactly 0.5 + 0.4*10*0.1 = 0.9 and 1 + 0.2*10*0.1 = 1.2, i.e. the ledger's own ceiling numbers. At mastery 9 they would be 0.86 and 1.18.

new_findings.text: The rendering constant that turns the 63x72 land mask into the board seen on film. WarSelectUI.as:233-234 places a war flag at `(terrx + TERRSHIFTX) * 10 + 4.5` , `(terry + TERRSHIFTY) * 10 + 8.8`, and :253-254 places the player marker at the same *10 pitch with +5 / +8.5 offsets. So one territory is a 10 x 10 px cell and the whole 63 x 72 mask draws as a 630 x 720 board - which is why the on-film War Room shows a uniform square grid ruled over a vector coastline. Together with the 735-pixel mask and the 21/51/8 shifts this is a complete, buildable specification of the board.
